# Instruction-only boundary assessment

These cases assess the instructions. They were not additional live tests.

| Boundary | Incomplete steps | Allowed report and cleanup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Profiler unavailable | Step 1 cannot capture the required signal. Step 2 cannot reduce a nonexistent artifact. Steps 3 and 4 cannot establish the required evidence chain. | Report the missing profiler and supported observations. Do not substitute a source guess or install tooling. Restore any authorized changes and reap only owned processes under step 5. |
| Valid profile, intervention forbidden | Step 3 remains incomplete. Steps 1 and 2 may complete. Step 4 may identify source, but it does not prove the mechanism. | Report the sampled hot path as a supported hypothesis, name the missing intervention authority, and preserve the profile. Do not mutate runtime state. Close owned inspector connections and reap only owned processes. |
| Source symbols unavailable | Step 4 remains incomplete. Steps 1 through 3 may complete if artifact capture, reduction, and intervention remain possible. | Report the artifact's available frame or script identity and the observed intervention, with an explicit attribution gap. Do not invent a source line. Restore probes and perform owned cleanup. |
| Unrelated live process | Step 1 lacks access authority if attachment was not authorized. Step 3 cannot mutate that process. Step 5 cannot stop or reap it. | Report the ownership boundary. Analyze an already supplied artifact only within its scope. Clean up the investigator's own clients and artifacts while preserving the unrelated process. |

owner.py.text:
import os, pty, subprocess, select, time, json, pathlib, re, signal
out = pathlib.Path('/tmp/jstack-runtime-forensics-20261016/output')
app = pathlib.Path('/tmp/jstack-runtime-forensics-20261016/app')
master, slave = pty.openpty()
command = ['node', '--inspect=127.0.0.1:0', str(app / 'preview.cjs')]
env = dict(os.environ, TERM='xterm-256color', NODE_OPTIONS='')
process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd=app, env=env, close_fds=True, start_new_session=True)
os.close(slave)
start = time.monotonic()
identity = {'pid': process.pid, 'ownerPid': os.getpid(), 'command': command, 'cwd': str(app), 'envOverrides': {'TERM': env['TERM'], 'NODE_OPTIONS': ''}, 'wallTime': time.time(), 'stat': pathlib.Path(f'/proc/{process.pid}/stat').read_text(), 'cmdline': pathlib.Path(f'/proc/{process.pid}/cmdline').read_bytes().decode().replace('\0', ' ')}
(out / 'identity.json').write_text(json.dumps(identity, indent=2))
buffer = b''
try:
    with (out / 'terminal.bin').open('wb') as terminal, (out / 'process-stats.jsonl').open('w') as stats:
        while process.poll() is None and time.monotonic() - start < 150:
            ready, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.25)
            if ready:
                try: chunk = os.read(master, 65536)
                except OSError: break
                terminal.write(chunk)
                terminal.flush()
                buffer += chunk
                match = re.search(rb'ws://127\.0\.0\.1:\d+/[a-f0-9-]+', buffer)
                if match and not (out / 'inspector-url.txt').exists():
                    (out / 'inspector-url.txt').write_text(match[0].decode())
            try:
                stats.write(json.dumps({'elapsed': time.monotonic()-start, 'wallTime': time.time(), 'stat': pathlib.Path(f'/proc/{process.pid}/stat').read_text()})+'\n')
                stats.flush()
            except FileNotFoundError: break
            if (out / 'stop').exists(): break
finally:
    if process.poll() is None: process.terminate()
    try: process.wait(timeout=5)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        process.kill()
        process.wait()
    os.close(master)
    (out / 'cleanup.json').write_text(json.dumps({'pid': process.pid, 'returncode': process.returncode, 'waitCompleted': True, 'procExistsAfterWait': pathlib.Path(f'/proc/{process.pid}').exists(), 'elapsed': time.monotonic()-start}, indent=2))

# Runtime forensics process

The authoring roots and instructions came from the caller. I requested the full parent mode before runtime work, but combined tool output truncated. I read the runtime-forensics playbook, control-cli, setup entrypoint and references, Codex system skill-creator, unslop, technical-writing, benchmark-checklist, Guard the Context Window, Explain the Number, Model the Domain, and Architect before launch. Targeted rereads recovered instruction text. A final read of parent-mode lines 130 through 165 occurred after cleanup and exposed the missed host-plan requirement. The full-read preparation was therefore not reliably complete before execution.

The data shape for the temporary driver is an ordered list of inspector actions with method, params, optional delayMs and output path. Requests correlate through a map of IDs to pending responses. The PTY owner records process identity, terminal bytes, periodic process stats and final reaping state.

The expected diagnostic claim is that a sampled callback runs while the terminal waits for input, and a reversible intervention changes its observed behavior. This is one controlled diagnostic run, not a production speedup comparison. Profiling and inspector overhead remain present. No exact function CPU duration will be inferred from sample counts.

The parent mode's general Architect trigger requests parallel design before code crosses function boundaries. The caller limits this test to one bounded reducer and prohibits nested evaluation. The temporary diagnostic driver therefore proceeds under explicit test authorization. Architect's parallel design procedure remains unexecuted. No product implementation or architecture is delivered.

The output report will be written directly from raw artifacts, with claims checked against protocol responses. Unslop and technical-writing guide the first draft. Later corrections will be recorded here rather than concealed as an initial draft.

The first report draft was written after live evidence, cleanup, and artifact verification. It included the diagnosis, counter observations, source mapping, ownership, and the host-plan timing failure from the start. The instruction-only boundary assessment was added at the caller's request without another live run. The report's profile counts came from the reducer, while protocol responses supplied state and source evidence.

This process note initially overstated that the full parent mode had been read before runtime. I corrected that statement after the post-run instruction audit. The host task list was created retrospectively with verbatim playbook text and completed diagnostic statuses. It cannot establish pre-execution planning compliance. The report does not claim full-mode compliance.

The final prose self-audit found no long-dash characters or promotional language in the report. No unslop cleanup rewrite of the report was performed. The direct first draft remains the delivered report. The child reducer's own writing process was not independently observed beyond its delivered artifacts.

report.md.text:
# Preview console runtime diagnosis

The preview console consumes CPU without terminal input because a timer calls `refreshPreview` every 20 milliseconds. The callback runs an arithmetic loop until its six-millisecond clock deadline. The live profile identifies this callback, the reversible intervention confirms its effect, and the live inspector source matches the source file on disk.

The source is [preview.cjs](/tmp/jstack-runtime-forensics-20261016/app/preview.cjs:7). Line 18 schedules the callback. Lines 9 through 12 contain the clock deadline and arithmetic loop. Line 8 checks `preview.enabled`. The profile reports script ID 87, zero-based line 6, and the same file URL. [verification.json](verification.json) retains the inspector's script metadata and matching SHA-256 hash.

The three-second [live CPU profile](baseline-profile.json) contains 2,718 samples. `refreshPreview` has 734 self samples beneath `listOnTimeout` and `processTimers`. Idle has 1,953 samples. Native `now` has 11 samples beneath `performance.now` and `refreshPreview`. These counts identify sampled activity. They do not establish exact CPU duration for the function. [reducer.json](reducer.json) retains the frames, ancestry, and validity checks.

The temporary inspector evaluation recorded the state, set `preview.enabled` to false, then restored its original property descriptor in a `finally` block. It collected one interval in each condition. No terminal input was sent. The frame counter stopped during the intervention and resumed after restoration. The whole-process CPU counters provide corroborating evidence.

| Condition | Observed interval | Frame delta | User-input delta | Process CPU delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enabled | 1,501.209 ms | 73 | 0 | 441,650 µs |
| Disabled | 1,499.402 ms | 0 | 0 | 10,682 µs |
| Restored | 1,500.462 ms | 73 | 0 | 450,123 µs |

[intervention-result.json](intervention-result.json) contains the raw snapshots and restoration result. [intervention-deltas.json](intervention-deltas.json) contains the arithmetic derived from those snapshots. This is one controlled diagnostic run, with one observation per condition and no repeatability spread. The process counters include instrumentation and unrelated runtime work. Disabling preview deliberately skips its work. These measurements confirm the mechanism in this fixture and do not establish a production speedup or an equivalent implementation improvement. The earlier profile and later counter windows are separate observations. The timer cadence and clock-bounded loop explain why the process consumes CPU while remaining idle between callbacks.

The owned process was PID 529457, launched in a PTY under Node v24.19.0 with inspector bound to 127.0.0.1 on ephemeral port 39769. [identity.json](identity.json) retains its command, working directory, process start identity, owner PID, and environment overrides. The inspector independently confirmed the PID and `stdin.isTTY`. [terminal.bin](terminal.bin) retains the ready prompt and inspector lifecycle messages. [process-stats.jsonl](process-stats.jsonl) retains process observations throughout the run.

The evaluation installed no global probe. Its local closures ended after the returned promise completed. The original enabled descriptor was restored, including its value and flags. A later inspection confirmed `enabled=true`, continuing frames, zero user events, and no global probe keys. The clients closed their WebSockets. The owner terminated and reaped the process after 74.247 seconds, before its watchdog, with exit status -15. The inspector port refused a later connection. [cleanup.json](cleanup.json), [final-runtime-state.json](final-runtime-state.json), and [verification.json](verification.json) retain these checks.

The app, README, caller note, and selected model configuration retain their original hashes. [hashes-before.json](hashes-before.json) and [hashes-after.json](hashes-after.json) show the comparison. All writes belonged to this output directory. No source fix, installation, configuration change, publication, schedule change, or unrelated process action occurred.

The five diagnostic steps completed. [playbook-status.json](playbook-status.json) preserves their exact text and retrospective statuses. The full-mode requirement to open the host task list before execution failed. I opened that list after cleanup. The completed statuses describe the diagnostic work and do not imply that this ordering requirement passed. Initial combined instruction reads truncated, so I reread the missing content in smaller reads. No runtime command or protocol request failed, and no diagnostic rerun occurred. All 15 inspector requests have successful responses.

The general Architect trigger also requested a parallel design procedure before writing code across function boundaries. The caller restricted delegation to one bounded artifact reducer and prohibited nested evaluation. I used the explicitly authorized temporary diagnostic driver and left Architect's design procedure unexecuted. This is a disclosed full-mode gap. The selected configuration did not change. [preflight.json](preflight.json), [thread.json](thread.json), and [reducer-status.json](reducer-status.json) record the reducer's inherited selection and completed terminal status.

Guard the Context Window kept raw profile arrays out of the conversation and assigned reduction to one bounded agent. Explain the Number restricted the counter claim to this controlled run. Model the Domain led to an ordered inspector-action list and a request-ID map in the temporary driver. Their exact authoring paths appear in [skill-manifest.json](skill-manifest.json). Unslop and technical-writing guided the report as it was drafted. [process-notes.md](process-notes.md) records the writing process and the later compliance findings.

No fix is included. The Bug fix and Perf issue procedures remain unavailable in this jstack package. The caller owns any subsequent decision about implementation, the pinned upstream comparison, and independent raw-evidence verification.

from pathlib import Path
import json,hashlib,collections,socket,urllib.parse
root=Path('/tmp/jstack-runtime-forensics-20261016'); out=root/'output'; dest=Path('/home/ubuntu/Dev/skills/research/jstack/evaluations/runtime-forensics')
def read(name):return json.loads((out/name).read_text())
def digest(p):return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
profile=read('baseline-profile.json')['profile']; nodes={n['id']:n for n in profile['nodes']}; samples=profile['samples']; deltas=profile['timeDeltas']
assert len(nodes)==len(profile['nodes']) and len(samples)==len(deltas)
assert all(i in nodes for i in samples) and all(d>=0 for d in deltas)
assert profile['endTime']>profile['startTime']
counts=collections.Counter(samples); frame=next(n for n in nodes.values() if n['callFrame']['functionName']=='refreshPreview');parents={c:n['id'] for n in nodes.values() for c in n.get('children',[])}
ancestry=[]; p=frame['id']
while p in parents:p=parents[p];ancestry.append(nodes[p]['callFrame']['functionName'])
assert ancestry==['listOnTimeout','processTimers','(root)']
assert counts[frame['id']]==734
assert frame['callFrame']['lineNumber']==6 and frame['callFrame']['scriptId']=='87'
assert frame['callFrame']['url']=='file://'+str(root/'app/preview.cjs')
assert read('live-script-source.json')['scriptSource']==(root/'app/preview.cjs').read_text()
identity=read('identity.json'); baseline=json.loads(read('baseline-identity.json')['result']['value']); intervention=read('intervention-result.json')['result']['value']; final=json.loads(read('final-runtime-state.json')['result']['value']);cleanup=read('cleanup.json')
assert len({x['pid'] for x in [identity,baseline,intervention,final,cleanup]})==1
phases=[]
s=intervention['samples'];assert len(s)==6
for first,last in zip(s[::2],s[1::2]):
 assert first['userEvents']==last['userEvents']==0
 phases.append({'phase':first['phase'].removesuffix('-start'),'frames':last['frames']-first['frames'],'wallMilliseconds':last['monotonicMs']-first['monotonicMs'],'processCPUUserMicroseconds':last['cpu']['user']-first['cpu']['user'],'processCPUSystemMicroseconds':last['cpu']['system']-first['cpu']['system']})
assert [p['frames'] for p in phases]==[73,0,73]
assert [x['enabled'] for x in s]==[True,True,False,False,True,True]
r=intervention['restoration'];assert r['descriptorBefore']==r['descriptorAfter'] and r['globalKeysAdded']==[]
assert final['enabled'] is True and final['globalProbeKeys']==[] and final['userEvents']==0
assert cleanup['waitCompleted'] and not cleanup['procExistsAfterWait'] and not Path('/proc/'+str(identity['pid'])).exists()
assert not Path('/proc/'+str(identity['ownerPid'])).exists()
endpoint=urllib.parse.urlparse((out/'inspector-url.txt').read_text()); sock=socket.socket(); sock.settimeout(1);code=sock.connect_ex((endpoint.hostname,endpoint.port));sock.close();assert code!=0

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess,json,hashlib,difflib
root=Path('/home/ubuntu/Dev/skills'); out=root/'research/jstack/evaluations/runtime-forensics'
base='572f067de8987943a77fde7faba247ed126c4040';cache='/home/ubuntu/.cache/jstack/upstream/upstream.git'
def git(*args):return subprocess.check_output(['git',*args],cwd=root).decode()
def upstream(pin,path):return git('--git-dir='+cache,'show',pin+':'+path)
def sha(s):return hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest()
def diff(a,b,x,y):return ''.join(difflib.unified_diff(a.splitlines(True),b.splitlines(True),fromfile=x,tofile=y))
m=json.loads((root/'research/jstack/upstream.json').read_text());old=json.loads(git('show',base+':research/jstack/upstream.json'))
expected=old;assert m==old
report={'base':base,'manifestCheck':'Manifest unchanged: watch roots, context paths, pins, reviewed checkpoint, decisions and mappings preserved','mappedSkills':len(m['skills']),'comparisons':[],'packageChecks':[]}
for name in ['jstack-juan-mode','jstack-setup']:
 row=next(r for r in m['skills']if r['name']==name); pin=row['adaptedFrom'];local=row['localPath']+'/SKILL.md';source=row['upstreamPath']+'/SKILL.md';a=upstream(pin,source);b=(root/local).read_text()
 report['comparisons'].append({'local':local,'source':source,'pin':pin,'upstreamSHA256':sha(a),'localSHA256':sha(b),'completePinnedDiff':diff(a,b,source,local),'baseDiff':diff(git('show',base+':'+local),b,base,local),'assessment':row['differences']})
 assert upstream(pin,'pstack/LICENSE')==(root/row['localPath']/'LICENSE').read_text()
 files=git('ls-tree','-r','--name-only',base,'--',row['localPath']).splitlines();changed=[f for f in files if (root/f).read_text()!=git('show',base+':'+f)]
 assert changed==([local] if name=='jstack-juan-mode' else [local,row['localPath']+'/references/configuration.md'])
 report['packageChecks'].append({'package':name,'licenseMatchesPin':True,'existingFilesCompared':len(files),'changedExistingFiles':changed})
row=m['skills'][0];source=row['upstreamPath']+'/playbooks/runtime-forensics.md';local=row['localPath']+'/playbooks/runtime-forensics.md';a=upstream(row['adaptedFrom'],source);b=(root/local).read_text()
report['comparisons'].append({'local':local,'source':source,'pin':row['adaptedFrom'],'upstreamSHA256':sha(a),'localSHA256':sha(b),'completePinnedDiff':diff(a,b,source,local),'assessment':'research/jstack/adaptations/runtime-forensics.md'})
report['upstreamPlaybooks']=git('--git-dir='+cache,'ls-tree','-r','--name-only',row['adaptedFrom'],'--',row['upstreamPath']+'/playbooks').splitlines();assert len(report['upstreamPlaybooks'])==23
report['localPlaybooks']=sorted(str(p.relative_to(root))for p in (root/row['localPath']/'playbooks').glob('*.md'));assert len(report['localPlaybooks'])==5
for path in []:
 listing=git('--git-dir='+cache,'ls-tree','-r','--name-only',row['adaptedFrom'],'--',path).splitlines();assert listing; report.setdefault('newContextSourceFiles',{})[path]=listing
f='skills/jstack/jstack-setup/references/configuration.md';report['configurationReferenceDiff']=diff(git('show',base+':'+f),(root/f).read_text(),base,f)
(out/'source-comparison.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+'\n')
print(report['comparisons'][-1]['completePinnedDiff']);print(json.dumps(report['packageChecks']));print('42 mappings; 23 upstream/5 local playbooks; manifest unchanged.')
